digo_source: Pakia (2005) App. III, App. V, App. VI
other_mijikenda: Swahili: shares the name mkuyu (Pakia App. VI)

teaser.en: A fig with leaves as big as dinner plates, often starting life high in another tree.

summary.en: *Chiuzi* is the giant-leaved fig, a large tree with huge leathery leaves and clusters of small yellowish figs. Digo also call it *mkuyu*, a name they share with the Cape fig.

about.en: *Ficus lutea* is a large, spreading fig tree with milky latex and very large, thick, leathery leaves, up to about 30 cm long. It often begins life as an epiphyte or strangler in the crown of another tree, sending roots down to the ground. The small figs are yellowish to orange-brown and grow in dense clusters along the twigs behind the leaves, where birds, bats and monkeys feed on them. Digo identify it by its leaves.

where.en: It grows in forest, riverine woodland and coastal bush across tropical Africa, from West Africa to Kenya and south to South Africa.

uses.en: Pakia records that Digo use the latex of fig trees (*Ficus*) to fix feathers onto arrow shafts; he doesn't name this species.

names.en: Pakia records two names: *chiuzi*, and *mkuyu*, which he also gives for the Cape fig (*Ficus sur*). *Mkuyu* is shared with Swahili, where it is a general name for wild figs. The existing reference also has a fig called *uuzi kaha*, *Ficus stuhlmannii*, so *chiuzi* may be a small form of *uuzi*, but Pakia doesn't explain it.

reason.en: Cape fig, which shares the name mkuyu
